title: Sarva Pindi
steps: Mix rice flour with soaked chana dal, sesame, crushed peanuts, chopped onion, chilli, curry leaves, cumin and salt. Add water to make a soft dough.
Grease a pan (traditionally a curved sarva). Spread a portion of dough, make small holes with fingers, and drizzle oil.
Cover and cook on low heat till crisp and golden on both sides.
Serve hot with chutney or tea.

fullIngredients.name: Onion, green chilli, curry leaves, cumin, salt

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Signature Telangana rice-flour pancake – crisp, spicy and unique in texture.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: The holes allow even cooking and crispiness.

title: Jonna Rotte
steps: Mix jowar flour with salt and hot water to form a soft, pliable dough.
Pat into thin rotis by hand (or roll carefully) and cook on a hot tawa till done on both sides.
Serve with spicy koora, pachi pulusu or any curry.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Staple millet flatbread of Telangana – gluten-free and rustic.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Best eaten fresh and hot.

title: Uppudu Pindi (Broken Rice)
steps: Temper mustard, cumin, curry leaves, chilli and onion in oil.
Add water and salt, bring to a boil, then add the broken rice while stirring.
Cook till soft and fluffy. Serve with chutney or pickle.

fullIngredients.name: Onion, green chilli, curry leaves, ginger
Mustard, cumin, oil or ghee, salt

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Telangana-style rice upma – light and comforting.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: A everyday breakfast in many homes.

title: Uppudu Pindi (Rice Rava)
steps: Temper mustard, cumin, curry leaves, chilli and onion in oil.
Add water and salt, bring to a boil, then add the rice rava while stirring.
Cook till soft and fluffy. Serve with chutney or pickle.

fullIngredients.name: Onion, green chilli, curry leaves, ginger
Mustard, cumin, oil or ghee, salt

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Telangana-style rice rava upma – light and comforting.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: A everyday breakfast in many homes.

title: Hyderabadi Mutton Biryani
steps: Marinate mutton with yogurt, spices, fried onions, ginger-garlic and herbs for several hours.
Partially cook basmati rice. Layer the marinated meat and rice in a heavy pot, add saffron milk and ghee.
Seal and cook on dum (slow steam) till the meat is tender and rice is perfectly cooked.
Serve with mirchi ka salan and raita.

fullIngredients.name: Yogurt, fried onions, ginger-garlic, biryani spices, saffron, ghee

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Iconic Hyderabadi dum biryani – the pride of Telangana.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Layering and slow dum cooking are essential for authentic flavour.

title: Hyderabadi Chicken Biryani
steps: Marinate chicken with yogurt, spices, fried onions, ginger-garlic and herbs for several hours.
Partially cook basmati rice. Layer the marinated meat and rice in a heavy pot, add saffron milk and ghee.
Seal and cook on dum (slow steam) till the chicken is tender and rice is perfectly cooked.
Serve with mirchi ka salan and raita.

fullIngredients.name: Yogurt, fried onions, ginger-garlic, biryani spices, saffron, ghee

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Iconic Hyderabadi chicken biryani – a lighter alternative to mutton.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Layering and slow dum cooking are essential for authentic flavour.

title: Pachi Pulusu
steps: Mix tamarind extract with water to the desired sourness. Add finely chopped onion, green chilli, curry leaves and coriander.
Temper or simply mix in roasted sesame-cumin powder and salt. Adjust with a little jaggery if needed.
Serve raw (uncooked) with rice or jonna rotte – especially cooling in summer.

fullIngredients.name: Onion, green chilli, curry leaves, coriander

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Unique raw tamarind soup/relish of Telangana – no cooking required.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Refreshing and digestive.

title: Gongura Mamsam
steps: Cook mutton with onion, ginger-garlic and spices till tender.
Separately cook and mash gongura leaves.
Combine the gongura paste with the mutton and simmer till the gravy thickens and flavours blend.
Serve with rice or roti.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Classic Telangana/Andhra-style mutton with sour gongura.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: The tang of the leaves cuts through the richness of the meat.

title: Hyderabadi Haleem
steps: Cook mutton, broken wheat and mixed lentils with spices and ghee for several hours, stirring frequently, till everything breaks down into a thick, porridge-like consistency.
Pound or blend slightly for the classic texture. Finish with more ghee and fried onions.
Garnish with fried onion, mint, coriander and lemon. Serve hot, especially during Ramadan.

fullIngredients.name: Ghee, fried onions, ginger-garlic, haleem spices
Mint, coriander, lemon, fried onion for garnish

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: GI-tagged Hyderabadi specialty – rich, slow-cooked and highly nutritious.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: The long cooking and constant stirring are key.

title: Bagara Baingan
steps: Slit and shallow-fry the brinjals. Prepare a rich gravy with roasted peanuts, sesame, coconut, tamarind and spices.
Cook the gravy with onion and ginger-garlic, then add the fried brinjals and simmer till they absorb the flavours.
Serve with biryani or rice.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Classic Hyderabadi vegetarian side – nutty, tangy and aromatic.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Often paired with biryani.

title: Sakinalu
steps: Mix rice flour with sesame, cumin, chilli and salt. Add water to make a soft dough.
Shape into spiral or concentric circles on a cloth or plastic sheet.
Deep-fry till golden and crisp. Cool and store in airtight containers.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Festive Sankranti snack of Telangana – crunchy rice flour spirals.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Long shelf life makes them ideal for festivals.

title: Punugulu
steps: Mix chopped onion, chilli, curry leaves and cumin into the fermented batter.
Drop spoonfuls into hot oil and fry till golden and crisp outside, soft inside.
Serve with coconut or peanut chutney.

fullIngredients.name: Onion, green chilli, curry leaves, cumin

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Popular street and home snack across Telangana and Andhra.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Great use for leftover batter.

title: Mirchi ka Salan
steps: Slit and shallow-fry the green chillies. Prepare a nutty gravy with roasted peanuts, sesame, coconut, tamarind and spices.
Cook the gravy, then add the fried chillies and simmer till they soften and absorb the masala.
Serve as a classic accompaniment to Hyderabadi biryani.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Essential Hyderabadi side for biryani – spicy, tangy and rich.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: The chillies should remain intact but soft.

title: Kodi Pulusu (Chicken Curry)
steps: Sauté onion, ginger-garlic and spices. Add tomato and tamarind extract.
Add chicken and cook till tender in a thick, spicy-tangy gravy.
Serve with rice, jonna rotte or roti.

fullIngredients.name: Red chilli, coriander, turmeric, garam masala

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Everyday Telangana-style chicken curry – bold and tamarind-forward.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Country chicken versions are especially prized.
